question: What are the two main sublayers inside a standard transformer block?
options: Multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network

question: Where do residual connections sit relative to the sublayers?
options: Wrapped around each sublayer: output = LN(x + sublayer(x)) (or pre-norm equivalent)
Between every parameter, never around sublayers
Only around the final block of the network
Only around the FFN, never around attention

question: Why is the same transformer block stacked many times rather than designed differently per layer?
options: Empirically, stacking identical blocks scales well and lets representations refine progressively
Different layers wouldn't fit on a GPU

question: Build a pre-norm transformer block by dragging the components into the correct slots, in order from input to output.
explanation: A pre-norm transformer block runs LayerNorm → sublayer → +residual twice: once around attention, once around the feed-forward. Pre-norm (vs post-norm) is the modern default because it stabilizes very deep stacks.
